verdict: READY TO MERGE - 7 of 8 findings resolved, 1 bubbled
strengths: No importer or runtime reference to dev2prod_DEP.py remains in the code at the head, so deleting the unused deprecated script cannot break run.py or the tests.
The deleted script carried a dead __main__ tail of commented-out debug code and a docstring naming a nonexistent `dev2prod` module; removing it clears that stale material.

The README tracks the code closely: run.py version forms, exit codes 0/1/2, the ERROR / NOT SHIPPABLE / Failed. ordering, the FPM_<version> folder naming, the HELP_ROOT versus DEST_ROOT behavior, the all-or-nothing archive rewrite and the glob matching rules all agree with run.py, prod_deploy.py and help_links.py.
The common-errors table quotes the real error strings from prod_deploy.py and help_links.py, each with a cause and a concrete fix.
Examples use `uv run` and absolute PowerShell commands, matching the uv environment (.python-version 3.14, pyproject.toml dev group) set up earlier on the branch.
The doc states the pitfalls a release operator needs: dirty tracked files are copied as they are on disk, nothing in the release folder is deleted, and a failed folder must not be shipped.

Suggested PR body: 'Add a usage README: setup with uv, how to cut a release (run.py, exit codes, common errors), fpm.env and fpm.json configuration, help-link swapping and HELP_ROOT, dry-run preview, changelog-to-Word conversion, adding another project, and a module map. Also deletes the deprecated dev2prod_DEP.py (611 lines; nothing imports it, run.py uses conversion/prod_deploy.py). Docs and deletion only; no change to the conversion package.'
The version forms, conflict handling and exit code 2 documented at README.md:45-67 match the argparse setup and `_resolve_version` in conversion/run.py exactly.

The folder-name rule (`v3.17.2` to `FPM_3_17_2`) and the help-link rewrite example (file:///E:/... to file://server/share/...) match `_generate_project_version_folder_name` and `Path.as_uri()` output for a UNC HELP_ROOT.
The dry-run error text quoted at README.md:158 is word for word the `_target_error` message in conversion/help_links.py, so readers can grep for it.
The fpm.json field table, including the `tracked_only` default and the glob rule for patterns with and without a slash, matches `ProdConfig` and `_matches` in the code.

The README is honest about failure modes: overwrite-without-delete, all-or-nothing archive rewrites and the NOT SHIPPABLE semantics are all documented, which most READMEs leave for production to discover.
Deleting dev2prod_DEP.py removes 611 lines of dead code that nothing imports, along with its commented-out debug block.

important.name: README lists dev2prod_DEP.py as a deprecated file that this PR deletes
important.summary:
README.md line 208 documents `dev2prod_DEP.py` in the Development path table as an earlier copier that is deprecated and not used by run.py. This same PR deletes dev2prod_DEP.py (611 lines removed, no head version; `git ls-files` lists only project_definitions/prod_deploy.json). At the merged head the README points readers at a file that does not exist. Nothing else in the code imports or references the module (grep finds only README and docs/PLANS historical notes), so the deletion itself is safe; the contradiction is the stale table row.

Also (docs): README.md:208 describes `dev2prod_DEP.py` as an 'Earlier copier ... deprecated, not used by run.py' in the Development path table. The same commit (8148af9) deletes dev2prod_DEP.py (611 lines), so at the head the file does not exist and the row points readers at nothing. The row also pairs it with `project_definitions/prod_deploy.json` as 'its config', but the deleted script never referenced prod_deploy.json (git grep on 8148af9^ finds no match), and no prod_deploy.env exists, so load_project('prod_deploy') fails; the JSON is an orphan definition, not the old copier's config. The file deletion is also not mentioned in the commit subject.

Also (roast): The Development table row at README.md:208 names `dev2prod_DEP.py` as the deprecated earlier copier, but this PR deletes that file (611 lines gone at 8148af9), so the new README's file map points at a file that no longer exists the moment it merges. The row also calls `project_definitions/prod_deploy.json` that copier's config. That is wrong too: the deleted script never read JSON (its settings lived in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`). `prod_deploy.json` is a ProdConfig-shaped definition with stale `source_root`/`dest_root` keys and no `prod_deploy.env`, so `load_project('prod_deploy', ...)` fails in `_load_paths`. A docs-only PR whose one deliverable contradicts its own diff.
fix: Edit README.md line 208 to drop `dev2prod_DEP.py` and keep only `project_definitions/prod_deploy.json` (deprecated config, not used by run.py), or remove the row if that config is also unwanted.
If the script should stay documented, restore dev2prod_DEP.py instead of deleting it.
Replace README.md:208 with a row for `project_definitions/prod_deploy.json` alone, described as an unused legacy definition with no matching .env (not loadable), or drop the row.
If the deletion was not intended, restore dev2prod_DEP.py in this PR and keep the row, correcting the 'its config' pairing.
Replace README.md:208 with: | `project_definitions/prod_deploy.json` | Earlier project definition; has no `prod_deploy.env`, so it cannot be loaded. Not used by `run.py`. |
If deleting `dev2prod_DEP.py` was not intended, restore it from 5232180 and keep the row, but drop the claim that `prod_deploy.json` is its config.

minor.name: Exit code 0 row and fpm.json sample promise more than they show
minor.summary:
README.md:65 says exit 0 means 'help links swapped', but the run also succeeds when the release holds no top-level .atbx or an archive holds no help links (_swap_help_links returns no error; swap_count 0 is not an error). README.md:119-129 shows fpm.json as if it were the file, but it drops most of global_denied, two of scripts' denied entries and the reference and tool_metadata folders from the tracked project_definitions/fpm.json, without saying it is an excerpt.

Also (roast): README.md:9 says the run turns `_debug_override = True` into `False`, and README.md:65 defines exit 0 as 'debug switch patched'. `_patch_debug_override` (conversion/prod_deploy.py:447-453) errors only when the target file is missing. If the regex matches nothing (the flag was renamed, reformatted as `_debug_override: bool = True`, or is already False), it patches nothing, adds no error, and the run prints `Success!`. So the README offers a guarantee that the code does not check.
fix: Reword line 65 to 'Every file copied, debug switch patched, and every help link in a copied archive swapped and shipped'.
Introduce the JSON at line 119 as 'an excerpt of fpm.json'.
Soften the README: line 9 'sets `_debug_override = True` to `False` in the copied package when present' and line 65 'Every file copied, debug switch patched when present, help links swapped.'
Or enforce it in code: in `_patch_debug_override`, append an error such as f"_debug_override = True not found in {target}" when `count == 0` in a real run, and keep the README as written.

minor.name: Common-errors row blames 'git not on PATH' on a message that case never prints
minor.summary: README.md:74 maps `git ls-files failed in ...` to 'SOURCE_ROOT is not a git repository, or git is not on PATH'. Only the first cause produces that text. With git missing, `subprocess.run` raises FileNotFoundError before any return code exists. `_load_tracked` (conversion/prod_deploy.py:375-379) catches it as OSError and reports `str(exc)`, which on Windows reads `[WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified`. The 'git' in the message comes from nowhere. Anyone searching the table for that line finds nothing.
fix: Split the row: keep `git ls-files failed in ...` for 'SOURCE_ROOT is not a git repository' and add a row `[WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified` | git is not on `PATH` | Install git or add it to `PATH`.
Or wrap the OSError in `_tracked_paths`/`_dirty_tracked_paths` so the message names git (for example 'git not found on PATH: ...') and document that text.

minor.name: env comment rule is narrower than the README states
minor.summary: README.md:81 says '`#` starts a comment'. _parse_env in conversion/prod_deploy.py (lines 51-66) skips only lines whose first non-blank character is '#'. A trailing '# note' after a value becomes part of the value (SOURCE_ROOT=E:/x # old would include the comment in the path).
fix: Say 'a line starting with `#` is a comment; trailing comments after a value are not supported'.

minor.name: Dry-run command prints a count, not the file list the prose promises
minor.summary: README.md:147-148 says the dry run 'list[s] what a release would contain', but the one-liner at README.md:151 prints only `len(r.copied)` and the errors. The listing the prose promises is never shown.
fix: Add `print(*r.copied, sep='\n')` to the command, or reword line 147 to 'count the files a release would contain and report its errors'.

minor.name: Changelog section overstates which empty headings are dropped
minor.summary: README.md:175-176 says 'An empty Unreleased section, empty subheadings ... are left out'. conversion/changelog_docx.py filter_blocks (lines 440-453) drops any empty level-2 release section (not only Unreleased) together with the subheadings inside it. An empty level-3 subheading inside a non-empty release is kept, so 'empty subheadings are left out' is wrong in general. Line 175 is also a single long line where the rest of the file wraps near 105 columns.
fix: Reword to 'Any release section with no content (for example an empty Unreleased) is left out with its subheadings, as is the Keep a Changelog boilerplate line', and rewrap the paragraph.

minor.name: Test section names two files out of nine
minor.summary:
README.md:193-197 ('Run the tests by file') lists only tests/test_prod_deploy_tracked.py and tests/test_help_links.py. tests/ holds nine test modules (changelog, run args, exit code, dirty, help root, fpm.json help pages and more), and pyproject.toml sets testpaths = ["tests"], so plain `uv run pytest` runs them all. A reader could take the two named files as the whole suite.

Also (roast): README.md:193-197 says 'Run the tests by file' and lists only tests/test_prod_deploy_tracked.py and tests/test_help_links.py. tests/ has nine modules, including test_changelog_docx, test_run_args, test_run_exit_code, test_prod_deploy_dirty, test_prod_deploy_help_links, test_prod_deploy_help_root and test_fpm_json_help_pages. All of them are self-contained and guard their own git or Windows skips. pyproject.toml already sets `testpaths = ["tests"]` so that the plan copies under docs/ are not collected. A plain `uv run pytest` is the correct command, and the documented one skips most of the suite.
fix: Add `uv run pytest` as the full-suite command and present the two files as an example of running one file.

Replace README.md:193-196 with 'Run the tests and lint:' followed by `uv run pytest` and `uv run ruff check conversion tests`, and optionally keep one 'single file: uv run pytest tests/test_help_links.py' example.

minor.name: Deprecated dev2prod_DEP.py removal is not covered by the commit message
minor.summary:
The only commit touching the deletion is titled 'Docs(readme): add usage README ...'. Removing the 611-line dev2prod_DEP.py (lines 1-611 at the merge base) is a code change that the commit subject and the PR text do not mention, so a reader of the history will not find it under a docs commit.

Also (roast): 8148af9 is titled 'Docs(readme): add usage README ...' but it also deletes the 611-line `dev2prod_DEP.py`. Nothing imports it; only the historical plan files under docs/PLANS/ mention it. So the deletion itself is fine, but someone reading the log will not find it under a docs title.
fix: State the dev2prod_DEP.py deletion in the PR description (one line), or split it into its own Chore commit.

Mention the deletion in the PR body. Suggested body: 'Adds a usage README covering setup (uv), release runs through conversion/run.py (version forms, exit codes, common errors), fpm.env path keys including HELP_ROOT and the help-link swap, fpm.json copy rules, dry-run preview, changelog-to-Word conversion, adding a project, and the dev test/lint commands. Also removes the deprecated dev2prod_DEP.py copier; nothing imports it.'
Or reword the commit subject/body to name the deletion (for example add a body line 'Remove deprecated dev2prod_DEP.py; unused by run.py').

bubble_up.reason: Fix is PR/commit text only. PR body now names the dev2prod_DEP.py deletion (developer-directed body); commit message rewording is the developer's call.
